name: TLC5947RHBR
title: 24-channel, 12-bit PWM constant-current LED sink driver with internal oscillator
summary: TLC5947 sinks a constant current of 2 mA to 30 mA on each of 24 outputs rated to 30 V, with a separate 12-bit PWM brightness for every channel run from a 4 MHz on-chip oscillator. Grayscale data is shifted in over SIN, SCLK and XLAT at up to 30 MHz (15 MHz chained), and one resistor sets the current of all channels. Thermal shutdown and staggered turn-on of four output groups are built in. It runs from 3.0 V to 5.5 V and comes in a 32-pin HTSSOP PowerPAD (DAP) and a 5 mm × 5 mm 32-pin VQFN (RHB); TLC5947RHBR is the VQFN on a 3000-piece reel.
key_figures: 2 mA to 30 mA per channel, set by RIREF

notes: All listed parts are active and in production.
Body size, nominal: HTSSOP (32) 11.00 mm × 6.20 mm; VQFN (32) 5.00 mm × 5.00 mm.

pins.name: OUT0
pins.function: Constant-current sink output, channel 0. Outputs may be paralleled for more current, and each output may sit at its own voltage.

pins.name: SOUT
pins.function: Serial data out, from a stage after the shift register's MSB, so the MSB is presented when SCLK falls; this reduces shift errors where the SIN-to-SCLK timing margin is small.

pins.name: XLAT
pins.function: Latch input. A rising edge copies the grayscale shift register into the grayscale data latch and turns all outputs off until the next display period begins. It does not clear the grayscale counter.

pins.name: IREF
pins.function: Current-set pin. A resistor from IREF to GND sets the sink current of OUT0 to OUT23.

pins.name: BLANK
pins.function: Blanking input. High: all 24 outputs off, the PWM timing controller is initialised and the grayscale counter is cleared to 0. Low: the outputs follow the PWM timing controller.

pins.name: SCLK
pins.function: Serial shift clock, Schmitt-trigger input. Each rising edge takes SIN into the shift register and moves the data one bit toward the MSB; the MSB is presented on SOUT at the falling edge. A rising SCLK edge may come 100 ns after a rising XLAT edge.

circuits.title: Typical application: daisy-chained TLC5947s
circuits.description: A controller drives any number of TLC5947s in a chain with four lines. DATA enters the first device's SIN; each SOUT feeds the next device's SIN, and SCLK, XLAT and BLANK go to every device in parallel. Every output sinks the current of a string of LEDs whose anodes go to VLED. Each device has its own RIREF to ground setting the current of its 24 channels, and a decoupling capacitor at VCC. The last device's SOUT is left open.

operation.text: TLC5947 has 24 constant-current sinks rated to 30 mA, each with its own 12-bit (4096-step) PWM brightness value. One resistor on IREF sets the full-scale current of all 24. The PWM clock comes from an on-chip oscillator of about 4 MHz, so no external grayscale clock is needed.

Grayscale data is held in a 288-bit shift register (12 bits × 24 channels) and a 288-bit latch. SIN enters bit 0 (the LSB end) on each rising SCLK edge; bit 287 is the MSB. Bits 0–11 belong to OUT0, bits 12–23 to OUT1, and so on up to bits 276–287 for OUT23; within each channel bit 11 is the MSB. The SOUT stage changes on falling SCLK edges. A rising XLAT edge copies all 288 bits into the latch, and the latch drives the PWM.

When BLANK goes low, each output with a non-zero latch value starts sinking on the oscillator's fifth rising edge. The 12-bit counter then counts oscillator edges and each output turns off when the counter reaches its grayscale value, or at 4096 counts. A value of 0 keeps the output off. The cycle repeats for as long as BLANK stays low, and BLANK high keeps every output off.
A rising XLAT edge turns all outputs off; the next display period then starts from the first oscillator clock using the newly latched data. XLAT does not clear the grayscale counter.
Display periods of 4096 internal clocks follow one another without any control signal, so the outputs keep running from the latched data until BLANK goes high.

The shift register and latch hold no defined value at power-up. Holding BLANK high until valid data has been written and latched keeps the LEDs from lighting at random. Where lighting at power-up does not matter, BLANK may sit at any level, and grayscale works through data writes alone even with BLANK tied to GND.
All outputs switch off at once when the junction passes T(TEF), 162 °C typical, and stay off while it is over that. They resume at the first clock after the junction falls below T(TEF) − T(HYS).

To limit inrush current and the noise it causes, the outputs switch in four groups of six with a short delay between groups: OUT0/4/8/12/16/20 first, then OUT1/5/9/13/17/21, OUT2/6/10/14/18/22 and OUT3/7/11/15/19/23. The stagger applies when switching on and when switching off; the delays are tD2 to tD4.
The resistor RIREF from IREF to GND sets IOLC for every channel by RIREF = 41 × VIREF / IOLC, with VIREF 1.20 V typical. IOLC is set between 2 mA and 30 mA.
Before a design starts, fix the highest current each LED colour needs, the highest LED forward voltage, and whether the auto display repeat is used.

VCC takes a 0.1 µF ceramic placed near the pin and the ground plane. VLED needs electrolytic capacitors spread evenly over the board, their number depending on panel size, and its ripple must stay below 5% of nominal. VLED must exceed the highest LED forward voltage by the output's knee voltage, 0.4 V at 10 mA.

Put the decoupling capacitor near VCC and the ground plane, and RIREF close to IREF and its ground. Make the ground copper as wide as possible for the large ground current. Keep each trace from an LED cathode to its OUT pin short and straight to keep inductance low. Lay out chained devices symmetrically. The thermal pad connects through vias to a heatsink layer.
Device dissipation, from the power dissipation equation, must stay under the package's rating at the ambient temperature.
Both packages have an exposed pad that must be soldered to the board for thermal and mechanical performance. On the RHB land pattern, any vias in the pad should be filled, plugged or tented.
